_: What each video says, beat by beat. `say` is spoken (spelled for the voice: agri-sim, kree-ging); `title` and `sub` go on screen. Every number comes from README.md (agribench runs) or from the recorded run itself. prepare.py turns `say` into runs/demo_video/voice/<id>.wav; a beat lasts as long as its voice plus a short pause.

explainer.title: Which part of this field is too dry?
explainer.say: Farmers usually water a whole field the same way. The dry patches only show once the plants are already suffering.

explainer.title: One probe. One spot.
explainer.sub: Every push into the soil takes 10 to 30 seconds.
explainer.say: A soil probe tells you exactly how wet the ground is, but only at one spot, and every push into the soil takes ten to thirty seconds. Nobody can probe a whole field by hand.

explainer.title: Every existing approach leaves a gap
explainer.say: Today's options each miss something. Fixed probes measure one point per zone. Handheld meters need a person to walk to every spot. Satellites see pixels of twenty metres or more. Cosmic-ray sensors average over a radius of more than a hundred metres. Tractors cannot drive through a standing crop, coring robots measure nutrients, not water, and scouting robots under the canopy estimate water stress only indirectly, if at all.

explainer.title: No product we found probes between the rows
explainer.say: Research robots that push a probe into the soil do exist, but they plan in open space, visit preset points, or skip mapping altogether. And hardware-first farm robots keep failing on cost: Mineral and Small Robot Company both shut down in 2024. So we prove the idea in simulation first.

explainer.title: What we built
explainer.say: agri-sim is a simulator of a planted tomato field. A small rover drives only in the lanes between the rows, stops, probes the soil, and turns a few dozen readings into a moisture map of the whole field, with its own uncertainty. agri-bench scores it against published methods, on fields nobody has seen.

explainer.title: It never touches a plant
explainer.sub: Lane centre lines only, reverse instead of U-turns, every pose checked against every nearby plant
explainer.say: The rover only drives on the lane centre lines, and reverses instead of turning inside a lane. Every pose is checked against every nearby plant. In fifteen thousand two hundred and thirty two benchmark surveys, it touched zero plants.

explainer.title: Each reading sharpens the map
explainer.sub: The robot's map, then the real moisture it never sees
explainer.say: Each reading becomes a coloured flag, and the map fills in between them by kree-ging. Here is the robot's map, and then the real moisture, which the robot never sees.

explainer.title: Probe for the farmer's decision
explainer.say: Our strategy, planned survey, first covers the field on a route that fits the mission deadline. Then it spends its last probes where a reading is most likely to flip a spot between too dry and fine. That is the decision a farmer actually makes.

explainer.title: agribench on fresh fields
explainer.sub: 0 = random probing, 100 = an oracle that knows the truth
explainer.say: On fresh fields, planned survey scores seventy five point eight out of a hundred. That is ahead of our re-implementations of spatial coverage sampling at sixty point seven, Moisture Mapper at forty eight point three, and greedy mutual information at thirty point six.

explainer.title: What agrisim checks, and what it lacks
explainer.say: In our comparison with the closest published systems, only agri-sim counts plant contacts, and lets the soil change during a mission, with rain and drying. What we do not have yet is a real robot in a real field.

explainer.title: AgriRover v2
explainer.sub: Designed from the physics; not yet built
explainer.say: The rover design follows the physics. The probe sits in an open bay between the axles, the only place where the whole weight of the rover resists the push. A rocker chassis keeps all four wheels on the ground, and the probe cleans itself after every reading.

explainer.title: Honest about what is left
explainer.say: Every soil number is still a placeholder until we calibrate with real field data, and our map error still ties the best coverage designs. Next come real data, a per-zone irrigation plan, and building the rover.

explainer.title: agrisim
explainer.say: agri-sim. Open source, and it runs on any laptop.

demo.title: Live demo
demo.sub: From one command to a field map you can explore
demo.say: Here is agri-sim running live on a Windows laptop, from one command to a field map you can explore.

demo.title: One survey, one command
demo.sub: planned_survey on seed 7: same seed, same numbers every time
demo.say: One command runs a whole survey: our strategy, planned survey, on seed seven. It prints the map error, how well the map finds the dry cells, the distance driven, and zero plant contacts. The same seed gives the same numbers every time.

demo.title: Add --view: the survey as a 3D replay
demo.sub: The intro panel says what you are looking at, in plain words
demo.say: Add dash dash view, and the same survey opens as a 3D replay in your browser. The intro panel says what you are looking at, in plain words.

demo.title: The six bars follow the probe cycle
demo.sub: lower, insert, measure, pull out through the brushes, blow dry, check clean
demo.say: The robot drives only in the lanes. When it stops, the six bars at the top right follow the probe: lower, insert, measure, pull out through the brushes, blow dry, and check it is clean.

demo.title: Each value lands as a ripple
demo.sub: the flag goes up and the map fades to its new picture
demo.say: When the value comes in, a ripple in the reading's colour marks the spot, a flag goes up, and the map fades to its new picture.

demo.title: D: drone view
demo.sub: a camera circling high above the rover
demo.say: Press D for the drone view, a camera that circles high above the rover while it works.

demo.title: The whole mission on one bar
demo.sub: a tick per reading, coloured like its flag; point to preview, arrow keys to jump
demo.say: The time bar shows the whole mission at once. Every tick is a reading, coloured like its flag. Point at it to preview a moment, or jump from stop to stop with the arrow keys.

demo.title: Judge the map against the truth
demo.sub: robot's map, real moisture, map error, uncertainty
demo.say: From above, the ground shows the robot's map. Switch to the real moisture to judge it, then to the map error, and to the uncertainty, which is lowest next to each reading.

demo.title: Click a reading to go there
demo.sub: the field from above and the 3D view share one selection
demo.say: The field from above shows the route and every reading. Click one, and the replay jumps to that stop, with the same reading ringed in the 3D view. The map error chart falls as readings come in, and plants touched stays at zero.

demo.title: Weather during the mission
demo.sub: rain shows on the time bar; a note says when it starts
demo.say: This survey has a rain shower. The time bar shows it in blue, and a note says when it starts. Rain makes earlier readings go out of date, so planned survey drives on rather than probe soil the rain is about to change.

demo.title: On a phone, one panel at a time
demo.sub: the same replay, laid out for a small screen
demo.say: The same replay works on a phone, with one panel at a time above the controls: what is happening now, the field from above, and the ground colours.

demo.title: Compare strategies on the same fields
demo.sub: agrisim bench: means with 95% intervals; every strategy keeps plant contacts at 0
demo.say: And agri-sim bench compares strategies on the same fields, with ninety five percent intervals, from one command.

demo.title: Try it yourself
demo.say: Try it yourself. Install with u v sync, then run one survey with dash dash view.
